problem_statement:
harden headless mode — OutcomeEvent, retry, cost routing, integration test

Phase 2 audit surfaced six gaps between the spec and the
shipped code. This commit closes all of them.

* OutcomeEvent: the loop now emits a terminal OutcomeEvent
  on the event channel with Kind, Usage, Turns, and Err.
  Every return path in RunQueryLoop routes through a single
  finalize() helper, so renderers can read the real terminal
  state instead of hardcoding 'end_turn'.

* jsonRenderer / streamJSONRenderer: both consume the
  OutcomeEvent and surface outcome, turns, and usage in the
  final document. stream-json also emits a 'cost' event so
  programmatic consumers don't have to scrape stderr.

* Cost stream pollution: cost.Summary() is now printed on
  stderr only in text mode. In json/stream-json it lives in
  the document and is suppressed from stderr to keep the
  pipe-clean.

* Transient-error retry: runWithRetry wraps the loop with
  exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s + jitter) capped at 4
  attempts. Retry-After is honored when present. CostTracker
  is reset between attempts so the final summary reflects
  only the successful attempt. Non-retryable errors short
  circuit immediately.

* End-to-end NIM integration test: new test in
  <file> wires openai.Client +
  query.RunQueryLoop + a hermetic httptest server to verify
  the tool-call round-trip across packages.

* README: rewritten with badges, feature list, configuration
  table, troubleshooting section, and an updated
  verification checklist.

* EffectiveMaxTurns helper added to Config (symmetric with
  EffectiveModel / EffectiveMaxTokens) with test coverage;
  local effectiveMaxTurns() in <file> removed in favor of
  the new helper.

report denied and unknown tools to the model and continue

executeToolCalls built is_error tool_results for permission-denied
and unknown tools, but when no tool actually ran the loop returned
end_turn without sending them. The model was never told, contrary to
the README, and a typo'd tool name ended the session.

Always append the tool_result message and loop; MaxTurns bounds a
model that keeps retrying. The existing permission-denied test
pinned the old behaviour and is updated to assert the fix.

parse flags anywhere and keep multi-word prompts

The stdlib flag package stops at the first positional argument, so
flags placed after the prompt (every README example, e.g.
forge -p "fix tests" --output-format=stream-json) were silently
ignored, and only the first word of an unquoted prompt was kept.

Split the arguments into flag tokens and positionals before parsing:
flags (with their values) may now appear anywhere, "--" ends flag
parsing, and the remaining words are joined as the prompt. Unknown
flags after the prompt are reported instead of becoming prompt text.

Adds table-driven tests covering the README invocations, multi-word
prompts, "--" handling and error cases; they fail on main.

anthropic adapter: signature routing, cache_control, ListModels, capability overlay

- Fix signature_delta emitting as fake text_delta (now routes to
  Thinking.Signature via accumulator)
- Add cache_control support on tools and assistant content blocks
  (previously system-prompt-only)
- Add ModelLister interface + ListModels on both openai and anthropic
  clients (GET /models, GET /v1/models)
- Add MergeWithKnown: live listing + curated overlay, no longer
  guesses capability flags from model-id substrings for unmatched ids
- Add ProviderNIM const, disambiguate NIM-hosted models from a future
  direct-OpenAI adapter in the curated table
- Consolidate LookupModel through findKnownModel so the two substring
  matchers cannot drift; pin agreement with TestLookupAndMergeAgree

retry re-issues the model request, never the tools

runWithRetry re-ran RunQueryLoop from the original messages after a
retryable error. A 429 that arrived after a tool ran replayed the
whole exchange: the tool executed again (side effects twice) and the
earlier history was dropped. The json renderer also kept the failed
attempt's error after a successful retry.

Resume from Outcome.Messages with the remaining turn budget, share
one CompactState across attempts, stop resetting the cost tracker
(completed turns were real spend), and clear the json error field on
each OutcomeEvent.

step 3 — Anthropic native adapter

New internal/api/anthropic/ package mirrors internal/api/openai/:
Client implements api.Provider, POSTs to /v1/messages with x-api-key
+ anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 headers, parses the SSE stream by
switching on the event: name. Adds the wire-shape details Anthropic
needs that OpenAI doesn't: top-level system field, tool results
nested in the next user message (no role:"tool"), flatter tools:
[{name, description, input_schema}] shape, thinking:
{type:"enabled", budget_tokens:N} with temperature/top_p unset when
thinking is on, max_tokens > budget_tokens (defensively bumped),
and Anthropic-specific stop_reason mapping (model_context_window_
exceeded → StopContextLimit, refusal → StopEndTurn, pause_turn →
StopEndTurn). List-of-blocks system prompts wired with cacheable-
block translation; cache_control emission itself deferred.

Anthropic model entries added to knownModels (every supported
generation gets the right capabilities — prompt caching + extended
thinking on the Claude 4 family).

internal/api/selector/ picks Anthropic vs OpenAI-compatible:
explicit cfg.Provider wins; otherwise cfg.APIBase matching
api.anthropic.com (scheme-agnostic, case-insensitive, host-exact)
selects Anthropic. Anything else (including the NIM default URL)
selects OpenAI-compatible — preserves existing behavior. Lives in
its own subpackage to avoid api ← selector → anthropic ← api cycle.

TUI (buildProvider) and headless (runHeadless) now go through the
selector. All 12 packages green on go test -count=1 ./..., go vet
clean, cross-compile produces 4 binaries < 9 MB each.

problem_statement:
save the session on exit

Three bugs kept the TUI from ever writing a session:

- RunProgram and both save helpers type-asserted p.Run()'s result to
  *Model, but bubbletea returns the Model value, so the save was
  always skipped.
- The helpers saved shared.messages, which only --resume sets. The
  live history is CmdCtx.Messages.
- saveResumedSessionOnExit read loaded.CreatedAt before checking the
  LoadSession error, a nil-pointer panic at exit when the resumed
  file is gone.

Accept Model and *Model (asModel), snapshot CmdCtx.Messages under the
shared mutex (historySnapshot, replacing lockMessages), check the
error first, and move the resume/fresh routing into saveFinalModel so
it is testable. Existing save tests now seed CmdCtx.Messages, the
real live source.

Tests: TestSaveSessionOnExit_AcceptsModelValue,
TestSaveSessionOnExit_SavesLiveHistory,
TestSaveResumedSessionOnExit_MissingFileDoesNotPanic (all fail on
main; the last one panics), TestSaveFinalModel_ResumedModelValueKeepsID.

never cut between a tool_use and its tool_result

CompactConversation cut at a fixed len-AutoCompactTailKeep. When that
index held a tool_result, its tool_use was summarized into the head
and the tail started with an orphaned tool_result (provider 400).

Step the cut back past tool_result messages so each pair stays in
the tail together.

add ReadSettingsFile, trusted_projects and flag provenance

ReadSettingsFile reads a single settings layer without creating
directories or substituting DefaultSettings, so a missing layer
contributes nothing when overlaid.

Settings.TrustedProjects (global file only; never overlaid) and
Config.PermissionModeFromFlag support the settings trust fix.

step 6 — multi-block MCP tool results via convertCallResult

Widen convertCallResult to handle MCP content[] arrays beyond plain text.
The text-only stub from step 4 joined blocks with newline; step 6 preserves
the full multi-block shape (text + image + audio + embedded-resource) so
the model receives image/audio bytes that step 4 would have silently lost.

- toolResultBlock gains typed fields (Type, Text, Data, MIMEType, URI,
  Name, Resource) plus a Raw json.RawMessage that UnmarshalJSON captures
  verbatim. A type alias avoids recursion on Raw's omitempty.
- toolsCallResult captures RawContent = json.Marshal(aux.Content) so
  convertCallResult can populate ToolResult.Blocks losslessly.
- Text is still the joined text blocks (downstream TUI summary / ToolEnd).
- Blocks carries the verbatim content[] when len(Content) > 0; the loop's
  three-branch serializer prefers Blocks over Text when set.
- Metadata exposes block_count and non_text_blocks for diagnostic reads.
- Fallback Text for IsError-with-no-content and non-text-only success so
  the model always sees something textual — no more silent '(no output)'.

4 new tests cover the multi-block path, image-only summary, text-only
pre-step-6 behavior, and the zero-blocks gate that lets the loop fall
back to Text-only serialization.

start /wait). The Cancel function sends CTRL_BREAK_EVENT to the

non-zero exit that resulted from our cancel signal is reported as
timed_out / cancelled, not exit code 1.

build-tag convention requires the platform tag immediately before

problem_statement:
step 7 — CLI --mcp-config wiring + settings layering

Wire the --mcp-config flag into ToConfig so the parsed Args populate
Config.McpServers, and let settings.json fill the gap when the flag
is absent. Per spec §2.3, the layered order is 'CLI flag > settings
.json > empty'.

- Args.loadMCPConfig reads --mcp-config and accepts either the
  canonical object form {"mcp_servers": [...]} (matches Settings) or
  a bare array. A *[]McpServerConfig pointer distinguishes 'key
  present with empty array' from 'key absent' so bare-array configs
  don't get misread as object-form.
- Args.ToConfig signature changes from (*core.Config) to
  (*core.Config, error). --mcp-config read failures are hard errors
  (exit code 2 in <file>) — silent fallback would mask a typo'd
  path. A missing flag is not an error.
- cli.ApplySettings adds the McpServers copy at the bottom: only
  fills cfg.McpServers when len(cfg.McpServers) == 0, so the CLI
  flag always wins.
- <file> handles the new error: prints 'error:' to
  stderr and os.Exit(2). Exit code 2 signals 'user-supplied flag
  failed' so shell wrappers can distinguish from generic failures.

Tests:
- 4 ToConfig tests cover no-flag (McpServers stays nil), object
  form, bare-array form, missing file (hard error), malformed JSON
  (hard error).
- 2 ApplySettings tests cover settings-fills-empty and CLI-wins.

Note on parse order: Go's flag package stops parsing at the first
positional argument, so tests pass --mcp-config BEFORE the -p
positional prompt. This matches the documented Usage ordering.

cap outbound frame size and avoid size arithmetic

Reject outbound bodies over maxFrameBytes, matching the inbound cap,
and append the newline via a capacity-capped slice instead of
make(len+1). Clears CodeQL's 'size computation for allocation may
overflow' alert and guarantees the caller's buffer is not modified.

step 7 — wire TUI into <file>

don't let repo settings escalate permissions or launch MCP servers

A repo-committed .forge/settings.json (or settings.local.json) could
set permission_mode and mcp_servers, overriding an explicit
--permission-mode and spawning arbitrary commands at startup.

- Project and local files are untrusted unless the project's absolute
  path is in trusted_projects in ~/.forge/settings.json. From
  untrusted files, permission_mode, mcp_servers, permission_rules and
  trusted_projects are ignored and a warning names them.
- An explicit --permission-mode / --dangerously-skip-permissions always
  wins over every settings file.
- Only existing files are layered, so a missing project/local file no
  longer resets global values to defaults, and .forge/ is no longer
  created in the working directory.
- Settings can only turn auto-compaction off, so --no-auto-compact
  works again.
- Running from $HOME no longer re-reads the global file as a project
  file.

keep compaction state across turns so the breaker trips

RunQueryLoop built a fresh CompactState inside the turn loop, so
ConsecutiveFailures was always 0 and a failing summarizer was called
on every turn (9 attempts in 9 turns, cap 3).

Hoist the state above the turn loop and add Config.CompactState so a
caller that runs one loop per user message (the TUI) can pass a
session-owned state. AutoCompactIfNeeded also honours Disabled.

  StdioTransport expects Content-Length frames, so no plugin could

+		}
+	}
+
+	// Update the status line so the user has visible feedback
+	// after the dialog closes. (The dialog itself disappears;
+	// the status line is the next thing they see.)
+	switch d {
+	case core.DecisionAllow:
+		m.Status = "Allowed: " + dlg.ToolName
+	case core.DecisionAllowPermanently:
+		m.Status = "Allowed (always): " + dlg.ToolName
+	case core.DecisionDeny:
+		m.Status = "Denied: " + dlg.ToolName
+	case core.DecisionDenyPermanently:
+		m.Status = "Denied (always): " + dlg.ToolName
+	}
+
+	if dlg.Respond != nil {
+		dlg.Respond(d)
+	}
 	return m, nil
 }

step 2 — file & search tools (Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep)

Step 2 of PHASE_3.md lands the five file/search tools the
agent needs to do real coding work. All five are pure-Go
(no shelling out to grep/find) so the tool set stays
hermetic on Windows and avoids the "user's PATH doesn't
have grep" bug class.

Tools (spec §3.2):

* Read — line-numbered file reader with offset/limit
  paging, NUL-byte binary sniff (first 8 KiB),
  directory-vs-file disambiguation. Default limit 2000
  (core.ReadDefaultLineLimit). Output is
  `{n}\t{content}` per line, 1-based.

* Write — full-file writer, MkdirAll on parent dirs,
  reports byte/line counts. Line counting matches
  `wc -l` semantics (empty = 0, "a\n" = 1, "a\nb" = 2).

* Edit — unique-substring find-and-replace. Rejects
  old==new and empty old_string. Uses the existing
  editutil.CountOccurrences (shipped in Phase 2) and
  enforces the spec ambiguity rule: count > 1 with
  replace_all=false errors out and tells the model to
  disambiguate. Preserves the file's existing mode on
  write-back.

* Glob — pattern matcher, up to 250 results sorted by
  most-recent-mtime first, returned as slash-relative
  paths. Hand-rolled `**` walker (stdlib filepath.Glob
  doesn't cross directory boundaries with `**`);
  non-`**` patterns fall through to filepath.Glob.
  Skips node_modules / .git / .svn / .hg.

* Grep — regex search (Go RE2) with three output modes
  (files_with_matches / content / count),
  head_limit+offset pagination, a `type` shortcut that
  expands to extension sets (js → .js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs,
  etc.), case-insensitive via inline (?i) flag. Skips
  hidden dirs and the usual build/dep dirs
  (node_modules, target, build, dist, out, vendor,
  __pycache__). Binary files skipped silently; per-file
  size cap 10 MiB.

  Known first-cut: context_before/context_after are
  accepted and threaded through but not yet rendered
  in content mode — documented inline.
